answer: One strong defence is a shard-quorum identity. Each newcomer splits its signing key into shards held by unrelated veterans scattered across the economy, like seeds across a meadow: no single holder can act alone, and a quorum must co-sign every new right the identity claims. Shards rotate each season by lottery, so a farm cannot gather its own keys in a frozen tundra of idle accounts. To forge a hundred fake identities, one operator must corrupt hundreds of independent holders at once, and any holder who signs for a fraud loses standing publicly. Forgery then costs more than it earns.
